questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted more practical experince in my academic work, since KU often offers courses that relies heavily on theoretical aspects. I, therefore, chose course such as conflict management and negotiation, that had a lot of practical work.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite hard. Italy is not known for being very structural, and we didn't get any information until quite late in the proces (some information, you also have to ask for yourself before getting it). The only orientation event that did occur was regarding social events outside of academia.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any. We had to find courses, their locations and their starting date by ourselves. But everyone had the same problems, so it was a good conversation starter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: You have to be looking in good time in order to find housing. The closer you are to your starting date, the more expensive are your options. And the pricing is in general quite expensive outside of the student residences. However, the student residences are much further away from the campus and they have quite bad transport options at night.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nobody lives on campus. I walked 30 minutes to school and that was just fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There needs to be more single rooms available in the student residences. A lot of people had problems with their roomates having different routines.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration is very flexible. You get a guide on how to do it and you can change your courses up until their exam dates. There also doesn't seem to be a cap on when the courses are full.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We got a guide on how to do it from our Erasmus coordinator through email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost everyone I talked to had to change their courses because they were overlapping. As exchange students, you take classes from different masters, meaning that they will likely overlap. Have this in mind, when looking for courses: It is good to have several prefered options!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get too attached to a course. It might be cancelled, be overlapping with other courses etc. Make sure to get pre-approval for a lot of different courses, that you are interested in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is easier than at KU. I think it is because the Italians' English skills aren't as good, and they therefore have it easier in English-spoken classes than in Italian-spoken classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more practical, which was what I wanted. There was more class exercises, presentations, roleplays, oral participation etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Conflict Management and Negotiation; Corporate Communication; Journalism, Media and Journalism; Digital Society.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all of them. Conflict Management and Negotiation was particularly fun, because you learn a lot about your personal conflict patterns and get to do roleplays. Digital Society is also very nice, because the American professor is super good at teaching and you learn a lot of exciting things on the societal impact of technology. Highly recommend!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Some social events, you have to pay for. Otherwise, it is mostly if you need house appliances that are provided in your household.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is as expensive as Copenhagen. However, drinks are way cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of universities in Milan, and therefore also a lot of different social clubs doing events. Most of them are only going to clubs however, be aware of this. The official event coordinators are ESN, but also clubs such International Week exists.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of fun going to Kings Pub every thursday with my friends, meeting other students and doing beerpong. It was with International Week, and in the beginning everyone was talking to everyone - a good place to make friends!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to cities around Milan! Especially Cinque Terra was beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I already have Italian friends from back home, so they introduced me to places, people etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the social events in the beginning of the semester! Everyone is meeting each other here.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Italian way is quite laissez faire. Everything is up to negotiation and never set in stone, making everything very flexible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming atmosphere. Everyone is welcome in the Italian families and at their dinners etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress, everything will work out just fine. Go to social events in the beginning and be open. Use your time to see the city and the people around you, school is less stressful than you think.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Porta Romana and Porta Venezia are the closest and nicest areas to live in.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting practical academic experiences. Also having Italian friends, getting their recommendations and going to Italian family dinners.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having enough time to do everything you wish to do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
